extraction.name: MMMU: A Massive Multi-discipline Multimodal Understanding and Reasoning Benchmark for Expert AGI
extraction.description: MMMU is a benchmark designed to evaluate multimodal models on massive multi-discipline tasks demanding college-level subject knowledge and deliberate reasoning. It includes 11.5K meticulously collected multimodal questions from college exams, quizzes, and textbooks, covering six core disciplines: Art & Design, Business, Science, Health & Medicine, Humanities & Social Science, and Tech & Engineering.
extraction.creator: Xiang Yue, Yuansheng Ni, Kai Zhang, Tianyu Zheng, Ruoqi Liu, Ge Zhang, Samuel Stevens, Dongfu Jiang, Weiming Ren, Yuxuan Sun, Cong Wei, Botao Yu, Ruibin Yuan, Renliang Sun, Ming Yin, Boyuan Zheng, Zhenzhu Yang, Yibo Liu, Wenhao Huang, Huan Sun, Yu Su, Wenhu Chen
extraction.citeAs: Xiang Yue et al., MMMU: A Massive Multi-discipline Multimodal Understanding and Reasoning Benchmark for Expert AGI, arXiv:2311.16502, 2024.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The benchmark collection takes three stages. First, common university majors were reviewed to select subjects where visual inputs are commonly adopted. Second, over 50 university students, including co-authors, specializing in these majors were recruited as annotators to assist in question collection. They collected multimodal questions from major textbooks and online resources, creating new questions based on their expertise where necessary. The annotators were instructed to adhere to copyright and license regulations. To avoid data contamination, annotators were advised to select questions without immediately available answers. The process resulted in a diverse collection of 13K questions. Data quality control involved checking for lexical overlap and source URL similarity to remove duplicates, format and typo checking by co-authors, and categorizing problems into difficulty levels, excluding very easy problems.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: College exams, quizzes, and textbooks from six core disciplines: Art & Design, Business, Science, Health & Medicine, Humanities & Social Science, and Tech & Engineering.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Data quality control involved two steps: 1) Identifying potential duplicate problems using lexical overlap and source URL similarity, followed by author review to eliminate duplications. 2) Distributing problems among co-authors for format and typo checking. 3) Categorizing problems into four difficulty levels and excluding approximately 10% classified as 'very easy'.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Problems were categorized into difficulty levels (very easy, easy, medium, hard). Approximately 10% of problems classified as 'very easy' were excluded. Questions were formatted into JSON files with fields for number, question type, question text, answer options, correct answer, question difficulty, and explanation. Images were stored as separate PNG files and referenced via file paths in the JSON.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Over 50 university students, including co-authors, specializing in the relevant majors were recruited as annotators. They collected questions from textbooks and online resources. Annotators were instructed to adhere to copyright regulations and avoid data from sites prohibiting copy/redistribution. They were advised to select questions without immediately available answers to prevent data contamination. Annotations included question text, answer options, correct answer, image types, question difficulty, and explanation. A secondary review team vetted annotations for quality and guideline adherence. Regular audits of random samples were conducted. Ambiguities were flagged for detailed review.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Over 50 university students, including co-authors, specializing in the relevant majors (Art & Design, Business, Science, Health & Medicine, Humanities & Social Science, and Tech & Engineering).
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset is available at https://mmmu-benchmark.github.io/. A live-updating leaderboard is available. The paper includes a version change log (V1 to V4) indicating updates to results and fixes to typos/URLs.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: MMMU aims to stimulate the community to build next-generation multimodal foundation models towards expert artificial general intelligence. It highlights challenges in expert-level visual perception and reasoning. The benchmark underscores the progress and challenges in multimodal understanding, indicating substantial room for improvement, especially in domains with complex visual input and heavy reasoning with subject knowledge.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The manual curation process may carry biases. The focus on college-level subjects might not be sufficient for testing Expert AGI. Models exhibit higher performance in disciplines like Art & Design and Humanities & Social Science where visual data is less complex, and lower performance in Business, Science, Health & Medicine, and Tech & Engineering which present more complex visual data and require intricate reasoning.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: MMMU is not a sufficient test for Expert AGI as defined by Morris et al., because there lacks a direct mapping between performance on MMMU and the '90th percentile of skilled adults,' nor are college exams the only tasks an AGI shall tackle. The manual curation process may carry biases. The focus on college-level subjects might not be sufficient for testing Expert AGI. Some image types (e.g., Geometric shapes, Music sheets, Chemical structures) show very low model performance, indicating poor generalization.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation, Fine Tuning. The benchmark is designed to evaluate multimodal models on massive multi-discipline tasks demanding college-level subject knowledge and deliberate reasoning. It is used to assess expert-level multimodal understanding capability of foundation models across a broad scope of tasks.
